verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both halves are present, each in the Lean's own variables. The implicit equation is literal (manuscript_coordinate_existsUnique, exponent 2h), and the elimination of η that yields it is forward_coordinate_identity. The derivative is given as the first entry of the Fréchet derivative of the two-variable map (q,z) ↦ (q - z²q^a, z) rather than as a one-variable ∂_q, and in the (z,q) variables: scalarSlope = 1 - 2h z² q^{2h-1}; scalarSlope_eq_L rewrites it to 1 - 2hη² at the coordinate point, which is the paper's value. The paper's middle term and the full chain are stated too: extended_L_lowerBound is 1 - a ≤ 1 - a·extendedEta², i.e. 1 - 2h ≤ 1 - 2hη² at a = 2h (and extendedEta = coordinateEta wherever τ > 0, by extendedEta_positive with positive_mem_domain), and extended_L_pos chains it to 0 < 1 - 2hη² exactly as the paper does; the same inequality appears in h, η notation as a step of TerminalPressure.logScaleDerivative_bound, and (privately) as SeedHandbackJets.L_lower. So the only reformulation is the packaging of ∂_q as the (1,1) entry of forwardMap_hasFDerivAt's triangular map. The Lean's hypothesis h < 1/2 (a < 1) is weaker than the paper's h < 1/100, and 1 - 2h > 0 is exactly h < 1/2, which is the a < 1 that supplies the strict end of the chain.
